reason: Independent clock audit contradicted the documented fixed-EST interpretation of HistData archives. On 21 September 2022 SPX and SPY minute returns aligned at a one-hour offset; European summer-time calendar rules also explained the March/November boundary pattern in the published USMPD window comparisons.
literature_corroboration: Kebe and Uhl (2024), High-Frequency Effects of Novel News on the EURUSD Exchange Rate, explicitly report that HistData has daylight-saving adjustments despite its fixed-EST documentation. This corroborates the documentation mismatch; the European calendar mapping used here is an inference from the independent clock checks, not a claim made by those authors.
clock_rule: Interpret each naive HistData stamp with Europe/London seasonal offsets, convert to UTC, then add five hours. Equivalently, add five hours in European winter and four hours in European summer. This maps the source clock to UTC; it does not mean that the source records London local time. No per-event offset selection is allowed.
scope: Apply one deterministic calendar correction to SPXUSD, NSXUSD and EURUSD and to both event and matched-control dates. Retain the documented-clock run unchanged in archive/documented-clock-run. All response definitions, rate-factor inputs, splits, sample gates, reporting rules and regression specifications remain unchanged.
chronology: The original held-out response run had already been examined when this data-quality failure was found. Corrected results are post-audit chronological transfer checks, not an untouched holdout or a prospective test. Refit on corrected 2018-2022 data and freeze that fitted model before recalculating corrected 2024-2025 predictions. Report both original and corrected chronology honestly.
limits: Independent intraday probes cover selected dates and instruments, not every observation. Aggregate agreement does not certify every minute. Further source errors and differences between provider quotes and exchange prices remain possible. No outcome-based event deletion or per-date alignment optimisation is used.
